description: Per-translation glossary overlay for the Wheel of Heaven Translation of 1 Thessalonians (canon-cited chapter 5; LWTE ch. 4 cites 5:1-3). Greek source conventions and chapter-specific lexical decisions. v1.0.0 (wave MC, 2026-11-02): 8 entries, all direct: the SBLGNT base-text and variant-reporting convention (NA28, Westcott-Hort, Tregelles, Byzantine and Textus Receptus kept distinct); theos 'God', kyrios 'Lord', names, and the scope rule for Hebrew-text central entries; adelphoi 'brothers'; 'Peace and security' (5:3); eidenai 'to respect' (5:12); pneuma capitalization; psychē 'soul' (5:23); the Raëlian-canon reception-note convention. Candidates for promotion to central with the Greek conventions of the other NT overlays once a cross-book Greek convention set is ratified. Wave MC signed off at human review on 2026-11-02 (zarazinsfuss); its central proposals were applied as central glossary v2.91.0 (New Testament), v2.92.0 (Septuagint) and v2.93.0 (Hebrew).

entries.source: SBL Greek New Testament (ed. M. W. Holmes, 2010) as printed base text; NA28, Westcott-Hort, Tregelles and the Byzantine text (Robinson-Pierpont) as recorded in the SBLGNT apparatus, and the Textus Receptus (KJV) as reported comparanda
entries.strongs: n/a (text-critical convention; variant units identified by verse)
entries.partOfSpeech: Overlay convention for base text and variant reporting in the Greek of 1 Thessalonians
entries.literal: Translate the printed SBLGNT text; report NA28 divergences, Byzantine readings and Textus Receptus (KJV) readings in commentary.
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 1901 follows the Westcott-Hort / Revised Version text, close to SBLGNT; KJV follows the Textus Receptus.
entries.wohChoice: The line translates the SBLGNT. Where it departs from NA28 (5:10 *peri* for *hyper*; 5:15 and 5:25 without NA28's *kai*), the commentary says so. Byzantine readings (Robinson-Pierpont, as recorded in the SBLGNT apparatus: 5:2 *hē*; 5:3 *gar*; 5:5 without *gar*; 5:6 *kai*; 5:10 *hyper*; 5:15 *kai*; 5:27 *horkizō*, *hagiois*; 5:28 *Amēn*) and readings of the Textus Receptus, identified from the KJV wording, are named separately; 'Byzantine' and 'Textus Receptus' are not used interchangeably. Readings of Westcott-Hort and Tregelles are reported where they differ (5:4 *kleptas*; 5:13 *en autois*). Manuscript witnesses are named only where a standard reference reports them (5:4, after Metzger); otherwise the commentary names the editions.
entries.rationale: The source file is the SBLGNT with its variant sigla removed, so the English must translate that text and no other; mixing readings from different traditions verse by verse would produce a text no edition prints. The same convention governs the corpus's other Greek books (overlay entries `sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation` and `critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`), so a reader meets one rule across the New Testament. The SBLGNT apparatus records, for each variation unit, the readings of Westcott-Hort, Tregelles, NA28 and the Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text, which makes those four comparisons verifiable; the Textus Receptus is not in that apparatus, and its readings are therefore inferred from the KJV and labelled as such. The founder-ratified discipline for the New Testament distinguishes the Byzantine majority text from the printed Textus Receptus, since they differ (in Revelation 5, for example, at 5:6, 5:7, 5:13 and 5:14), and the convention keeps the two apart. Named scholarship: M. W. Holmes, *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (2010), apparatus; B. M. Metzger, *A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament*, 2nd ed. (1994); M. A. Robinson and W. G. Pierpont, *The New Testament in the Original Greek: Byzantine Textform* (2005).

entries.source: θεός; κύριος; Ἰησοῦς Χριστός; ἡμέρα κυρίου
entries.translit: theos; kyrios; Iēsous Christos; hēmera kyriou
entries.partOfSpeech: Overlay convention: divine names and titles in the Greek of 1 Thessalonians; scope rule for Hebrew-text central entries
entries.literal: god, God; lord, master, Lord; Jesus Christ; day of the Lord
entries.standardEnglish: God; the Lord; Jesus Christ; the day of the Lord (KJV, ASV, RSV, NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'God' for *theos* (5:9, 18; 5:23 'the God of peace'); 'Lord' for *kyrios* (5:2 'the day of the Lord'; 5:9, 23, 28 'our Lord Jesus Christ'; 5:12 'in the Lord'; 5:27 'by the Lord'); 'Jesus' and 'Christ' under the central `iēsous-yehoshua-yhwh-saves-folk-etymology-cross-corpus` and `christos-māšîaḥ-anointed-one-cross-corpus-greek-hebrew-aramaic`. Central entries written for the Hebrew text that transliterate YHWH or keep *Elohim* (including the *yôm YHWH* material) are background and are not applied: *hēmera kyriou* is the Septuagint's form of *yôm YHWH*, but the Greek does not carry the name.
entries.rationale: The founder-ratified convention for the corpus's Greek New Testament books renders *theos* 'God' and *kyrios* 'Lord', as in Matthew, Mark, Luke, Acts and Revelation (revelation-woh overlay `theos-god-rendering-against-canon-english-yahweh-revelation`). In the Septuagint *kyrios* stands for the Tetragrammaton and *theos* for *ʾĕlōhîm*, but neither Greek word carries the Hebrew form, so writing 'YHWH' or 'Elohim' in a Greek line would add information the source does not contain (BDAG s.vv.; TDNT 3, s.v. *kyrios*). The project's Hebrew books transliterate the name because their source distinguishes it; that evidence lies in the Hebrew, and the Hebrew-text entries stay with the Hebrew lines, with their cross-corpus links recorded in commentary. 'the day of the Lord' is the form of every major English version and keeps the link to the prophetic *yôm YHWH* visible through the commentary at 5:2 rather than in the line.

entries.partOfSpeech: noun, masculine plural (vocative of address; accusative and dative)
entries.literal: brothers; fellow members of the community
entries.wohChoice: 'brothers' in address (5:1, 4, 12, 14, 25) and in 'all the brothers' (5:26, 27), as in the corpus's other Greek books (Matt 23:8; Rev 6:11). That the address includes the women of the assembly is stated in the commentary at 5:1, not added to the line.
entries.rationale: *adelphoi* is a masculine plural which, used of a community, includes its women members (BDAG s.v. *adelphos* 2a); the Thessalonian assembly included women (Acts 17:4). 'brethren' is archaic, and 'brothers and sisters' (NRSV) adds a word that the Greek does not contain. 'brothers' is the formal equivalent (as in the ESV), and the corpus's Greek books already render *adelphos* 'brother(s)' (Matthew 23:8 'you are all brothers'; Revelation 6:11 'their brothers'). The inclusive sense is therefore given once in the commentary, and the line keeps the formal equivalent.

entries.standardEnglish: 'Peace and safety' (KJV, ASV, NIV); 'There is peace and security' (RSV, NRSV, ESV)
entries.wohChoice: 'Peace and security'. The ASV and KJV 'safety' and the imperial-slogan and prophetic backgrounds are given in the commentary; the canon's agreeing wording is recorded in the reception note.
entries.rationale: *asphaleia* covers 'safety, security, stability' (BDAG s.v. *asphaleia*; LSJ), so both English renderings are lexically sound and both are used by major versions. 'security' is chosen because many commentators read the pair against the Roman imperial theme *pax et securitas* (H. Koester, 'Imperial Ideology and Paul's Eschatology in 1 Thessalonians', in R. A. Horsley, ed., *Paul and Empire*, 1997; J. A. D. Weima, *1-2 Thessalonians*, BECNT, 2014), and 'security' is the English that keeps that public, political sense, while still fitting the alternative reading of an echo of the false prophets' 'Peace, peace' (Jer 6:14; 8:11; Ezek 13:10). The Raëlian canon cites this passage as « la paix » et « la sécurité » (*Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials*, ch. 4; English edition 'peace and security'); that agreement is recorded in the reception note and is not the ground of the decision, which would stand without it. The entry is direct: it adopts the rendering of the RSV, NRSV and ESV and records the ASV alternative.

entries.partOfSpeech: verb, perfect infinitive with present sense
entries.standardEnglish: 'to know' (KJV, ASV); 'to respect' (RSV, NRSV, ESV); 'to acknowledge' (NIV)
entries.wohChoice: 'to respect those who labor among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you'.
entries.rationale: With a personal object and in the context of honouring leaders (v 13 'to esteem them very highly in love'), *eidenai* means 'recognize the worth of, respect' (BDAG s.v. *oida*, where this verse is cited for that sense; cf. Ignatius, *Smyrnaeans* 9:1). The ASV and KJV 'to know' is a word-for-word rendering, but in modern English it reads as 'be acquainted with', which the Thessalonians already were, so it obscures what Paul asks. The RSV, NRSV and ESV render 'respect', and the major commentaries agree (Malherbe, AB 32B, 2000; Wanamaker, NIGTC, 1990, ad loc.). The literal 'know' is given in the commentary.

entries.standardEnglish: 'the Spirit' (5:19, ASV, KJV, RSV, NRSV); 'your spirit' (5:23, all major versions)
entries.wohChoice: Capital 'Spirit' for God's *pneuma* (5:19 'Do not quench the Spirit'); lower case for the human spirit (5:23 'your spirit and soul and body'), as in the Matthew overlay entry `pneuma-spirit-capitalization-matthew`.
entries.rationale: At 5:19 *to pneuma* stands beside prophecy (v 20) and is the Spirit given by God that the letter has already named (1:5-6 'in the Holy Spirit'; 4:8 'God, who gives his Holy Spirit to you'); the verb *sbennymi* 'quench' pictures it as a fire. At 5:23 *hymōn to pneuma* has a possessive and is listed with soul and body, so it is the human spirit. The same split is made in the published Matthew chapters and in every major English version, and the capital marks a distinction the context makes, not a doctrinal addition (BDAG s.v. *pneuma*; Malherbe, AB 32B, ad loc.). The Genesis central entry `ruach-elohim` governs the Hebrew phrase of Gen 1:2 and is not applied.

entries.literal: life, breath of life; the inner self, soul
entries.wohChoice: 'soul' where *psychē* is listed with *pneuma* and *sōma* (5:23 'your spirit and soul and body'). Elsewhere in the letter, outside this chapter, *psychē* can mean 'life' or 'self' (2:8).
entries.rationale: *psychē* renders Hebrew *nepeš* in the Septuagint and keeps its range, physical life and the inner person (BDAG s.v. 1, 2). In a list with 'spirit' and 'body', the inner person is meant, and 'soul' is the English word every major version uses; 'life' would break the list. The Matthew overlay entry `psyche-soul-life-matthew` makes the same context-sensitive split, and the commentary at 5:23 notes that the triad is generally read as a way of naming the whole person (Malherbe, AB 32B; Wanamaker, NIGTC), so the rendering adds no anthropology of its own.

entries.source: (convention entry: 1 Thessalonians verses cited in The Book Which Tells the Truth, Extraterrestrials Took Me to Their Planet and Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials)
entries.wohChoice: At every verse quoted, paraphrased or cited by reference in the first three Raëlian books, the commentary ends with a separately headed paragraph, '**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).**', giving the book and chapter, the canon's wording (French original and English edition) and the reading it attaches. For a range citation (LWTE ch. 4, 1 Thess 5:1-3) the full note stands at the verse that contains the quoted words (5:3), and the other verses carry a short pointer. Where the line and the canon agree (5:3 'Peace and security'), the agreement is recorded and the ground of the line is stated separately.
entries.rationale: This is the framework already used in the corpus's other Greek books (matthew-woh `raelian-canon-citation-reception-note-convention-matthew`; the reception notes of the published Revelation chapters). Keeping the reception reading in a separate, labelled paragraph lets a reader see exactly where the Wheel of Heaven reading enters the apparatus, and ensures that it never enters the English line. The canon citation was checked against the program's text of *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* ch. 4 (LWTE-4:90).
